SEAT VERDICT: R4-NF1 IS DISCHARGED. GO from this seat. No P1, P2, or P3 survives execution. Five P4s, none blocking.

WORKSPACE: <build-scratch>/nf1.771F8J (fresh clone + 8 mutant scripts under mut/). Nothing was pushed, commented, or written to GitHub. Every load-bearing claim below was re-executed from primary sources: live GitHub REST, git objects in a fresh clone, and the repo's own scripts.

=== THE CORE RESULT ===
The rc4 NO-GO's decider was: six commits in PR #197's range carry no Signed-off-by, so DCO lands red at ready-mark. I re-executed the oracle end to end:
- main@13f1ad7's shipped unsigned_commits(), run over PR #197's LIVE 31-commit REST list, returns [] — ZERO.
- The copy CI executes is the BASE revision's: dco.yml is pull_request_target with `ref: base.sha`, and PR #197's base.sha is 13f1ad7 = current main HEAD = the merge of repair PR #198. PR #198 landed 18:58:35Z; the DCO run started 19:18:32Z; main has not moved since. The timing forecloses the "ran against a stale base" failure mode.
- Live: PR #197 draft=False, DCO run 32292298616 conclusion=success, and step [4] 'Require author-matching Signed-off-by lines' is completed/SUCCESS — it EXECUTED. The green is not a skipped-gate artifact.
- All 13 workflow runs and 18 check-runs at C+1: none red.

=== SOUNDNESS, NOT MERELY EFFECTIVENESS (the question this seat exists to ask) ===
The strongest result I obtained is that the attestation is EXACTLY MINIMAL AND EXACTLY SUFFICIENT, which rules out a smuggled SHA:
- Dropping any one of the five causes exactly that commit to be caught (5/5 individually necessary — so no entry is decorative, and every entry is provably inside PR #197's range).
- Emptying the dict catches exactly those same five and no others (so the list is not over-broad).
- git objects independently confirm all five are parents=1, sob_lines=0, authored by 'Cursor Agent <cursoragent[at]cursor.com [address redacted: public-content gate]>', and still ancestors of C+1 — history was not rewritten, so the three prior verdicts and pin tags remain valid.
- Member-for-member match against the digests the rc4 arbitration itself named (lines 114/154).
The repair is also the exact remedy the rc4 letter prescribed in option (b), not a substitute for it.

=== WHAT I TRIED TO BREAK AND COULD NOT ===
I ran 8 source mutations and an 11-case adversarial input battery specifically hunting for a fail-open. Six mutations were killed by the self-test; forcing either unsigned merge to one parent makes it caught, proving the merge limb is load-bearing rather than decorative; and the checker is fail-CLOSED on every degenerate input I could construct (missing sha, missing parents, missing commit/author keys, empty author identity, quoted-text signoff, committer-not-author signoff, uppercase SHA). Two pass-throughs are deliberate policy (case-insensitive matching; octopus merges), not defects. I found no way to make an unsigned authored commit pass.
Two further assurances beyond the brief: the repair is itself SEALED (check_dco.py, dco.yml and test_check_dco.py are all inventoried with matching sha256 digests, so future main-side drift trips R5 DIGEST MISMATCH rather than silently changing the candidate's DCO verdict), and the checker has a SECOND independent test surface (test_check_dco.py, 4 tests, wired into epistemic-flexibility.yml:136 and PASSing in clean-baseline.json).

=== WHAT I DID FIND (all P4, none blocking) ===
NF1-V1 is the one the brief predicted and it is real: `attested = sorted(ATTESTED_UNSIGNED)[0]` makes the "attested commit is exempt" control self-referential. Delete an attested entry and the self-test stays green (mutation M1 survived, exit 0) while the live check correctly goes red. The control proves the mechanism, never the contents — so "seven planted controls" overstates what control #5 guards. It does not touch the discharge, because the contents oracle is the live PR check and I executed it, but a future bad edit to the list would not be caught by the step advertised as guarding it. Note M8 (deleting the 40-hex assertion) also survived, but that survival is correct by construction — an assertion cannot change behavior on input that does not violate it — and M2 proved that assertion genuinely fires.
NF1-V2 grades the loosening honestly: inside PR #197 it exempts nothing anyone would want certified (all three merges have empty combined diffs), but repo-wide e7de3637 is a genuine unsigned "evil merge" carrying 20 lines of authored prose into helix/SKILL.md. It is an ancestor, out of range, and the limit is disclosed in both the code and D18 — hence P4, not higher. I deliberately did not inflate it.
NF1-V3: the rc5 delta added a SEVENTH unsigned commit (merge 375973c9) after D18 declared the list closed. It rides the merge limb, is a clean merge, and violates no letter — but it shows the exemption is a standing channel, and D18's own `git merge --signoff` advice went unapplied.
NF1-V4 is cosmetic (comment says "five" then "six" over five entries). NF1-V5 is a latent 250-commit pagination fail-open in github_commits(), pre-existing and inapplicable at 31 commits; I report it only because I am certifying that oracle.

=== BLOCKED (2, both mitigated, neither load-bearing) ===
Branch-protection enumeration (403 unauthenticated) and raw run-log download (403 via proxy). I did not treat either as a pass. For the first I substituted the repo's own policy letter, RELEASING.md gate 5, and checked the single skipped job (contract-macos) against its skipped-step clause — it is dispatch-only by an explicit workflow `if:` and disclosed in KL-MACOS-162, so the skip is licensed. For the second, the jobs API is the same GitHub-side primary record and gives step-level conclusions, and I reproduced the script's verdict locally over the identical live input. Independently relevant: the rc4 panel recorded branch-protection enforcement as "off", so GitHub mechanics were never the binding constraint — the repo's policy letter is, and it is satisfied.

"PR #197 is READY and all required checks green at C+1" — verified independently, true. The four non-DCO run IDs the dispatcher labelled "stdlib/custody-style/contract/build" have IDs numerically LOWER than the DCO run, which I flagged as a possible misattribution to the 19:17 skipped batch; on fetching each, all four are in fact the 19:18:31 ready-mark batch, all success at head 546ccc8e, all with zero skipped steps.
